title: 9.5 Derivatives of Vector Functions; Arc Length

icans: I can find the domain and limit of a vector function.
I can differentiate a vector function component by component.
I can find the arc length of a vector function.

vocab: a function whose __________ is a vector, such as r(t) with components x(t) and y(t)
r′(t) = ⟨x′(t), y′(t)⟩, a __________ vector to the curve

blocks.sec: Part 2 · Notes and examples (fill in each note, then work the example)

notes: Domain: the values of t where every _______________ is defined.

blocks.stem: Find the domain of r(t) = ⟨√(4 − t), ln(t + 2)⟩.
Find the limit of ⟨(t² − 4)/(t − 2), t² + 1⟩ as t → 2.
Find the arc length of r(t) = ⟨3 cos t, 3 sin t⟩, 0 ≤ t ≤ π.

(AP® Practice) The limit of ⟨t, (t² − 2t)/(t − 2)⟩ as t → 2 is
(A) ⟨2, 2⟩   (B) ⟨2, 0⟩   (C) ⟨0, 2⟩   (D) The limit does not exist.

tickets.stem: Find the domain of ⟨√(3 − t), ln(t + 1)⟩.
Write the arc length formula for r(t).
